newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhstan says Deutsche Telekom talks difficult.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhstan says Deutsche Telekom talks difficult.

text.p: Kazakhstan has run into difficulties in talks about selling Deutsche Telekom AG 49 percent of state telecoms firm Kaztelekom because the German company wants a monopoly over Kazakhstan's present and future telecoms services, a senior Kazakh official said on Thursday.
As a result, the expected signing of the contract has been delayed, State Property Committee chairman Sarybai Kalmurzayev told a news conference.

"One of the unacceptable terms, put forward by Deutsche Telekom...is to have an exclusive right both for the current telecommunications servicfor those which may appear on the part of Kazakhstan in future," he said.
There were also difficulties of a technical character, he said.
In May Kazakhstan said Deutsche Telekom had agreed in principle to buy 49 percent of Kaztelekom and take management control for up to 15 years.

Kalmurzayev's office said Deutsche Telekom had promised to invest 825 million marks on paying off Kaztelekom's debts, increasing the number of lines by 50 percent over five years and doubling them in 10 years.
Deutsche Telekom, however, has never publicly commented on the Kaztelekom negotiations, and again declined to do so when contacted by Reuters in Germany on Thursday.
Kalmurzayev said the Kazakh government planned to write to Deutsche Telekom management about the problem.
"We are continuing talks with Deutsche Telekom, because the technology, reputation and might of Deutsche Telekom will enable us to lead Kaztelekom to the international market," he said.
He said other foreign companies had shown interest in buying Kaztelekom shares.
